Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.

If the code is single-threaded, this will lead to a significant under-utilization of resources, with 3 cores remaining idle for each of the 7 serial executions.

The script runs the exact same python command seven times in a row. This is highly redundant and may be an error in the original script. A for-loop would be a more conventional way to repeat a command.
The script contains multiple hardcoded, user-specific paths for the output file and the python script, which makes it non-portable.
